info.name: Wikimedia Enterprise APIs
info.description:
The Wikimedia Enterprise APIs give you high-volume, read-only access to Wikipedia and other [supported Wikimedia projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/). Use this collection to try every endpoint in version 2.0.1 of the API before you write code.

# Get started

1. **Create an account.** [Sign up for a free account](https://dashboard.enterprise.wikimedia.com/signup/) and verify your email. No credit card is required.
2. **Store your credentials in Postman Vault.** Your local vault keeps them encrypted and doesn't sync them to the Postman Cloud. Click **Vault** in the footer of the Postman window. If Postman asks you to create a vault key, keep a copy in your password manager. Then click **Add new secret** and create two secrets:
    - `wmeUsername`: your Wikimedia Enterprise username, in lowercase
    - `wmePassword`: your Wikimedia Enterprise password

    In **Allowed domains**, enter `https://auth.enterprise.wikimedia.com` for both.
3. **Let the collection read the vault.** In the vault, click **Settings** and turn on **Allow Vault secrets in scripts**.
4. **Send your first request.** Open **Metadata > Projects Available** and click **Send**. When Postman asks "Grant Vault access for this execution?", keep **Only this collection** selected and click **Grant Access**.

That's all the setup. The collection logs in before your requests and refreshes your access token when it needs to, so you don't need to run **Authentication > Login** or set up an environment.

# Choose an API

- **[Snapshot API](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/):** every article in a project, downloaded as one compressed file. Use it to work with a whole project, such as all of English Wikipedia.
- **[On-demand API](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/):** the current version of a single article, by name. Use it when you need specific articles.
- **[Realtime API](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/realtime/):** updates as they happen, as a stream or as hourly **Realtime: Batch** files. It requires a paid account.

Beta requests for Structured Contents and Wikidata are in the folders of the APIs that offer them. For help deciding, see [Choose the right API for the job](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/best-practices/#choose-the-right-api-for-the-job).

# Try these requests

To set a value like `{{articlename}}`, hover over it in the request URL and type in the box that appears.

- **On-demand API > Article Lookup:** set `{{articlename}}` to `NASA` to get the article from English Wikipedia.
- **Snapshot API > Snapshot Info:** set `{{snapshot_identifier}}` to `enwiki_namespace_0` to see the size and date of the English Wikipedia snapshot before you download it.

# If a request fails

- **"Wikimedia Enterprise credentials not found":** check that both secrets exist with exactly those names (step 2) and that **Allow Vault secrets in scripts** is on (step 3).
- **You chose Deny Access by mistake:** in the vault, open **Settings**, then the **Manage access** tab, and click **Grant Access** next to the collection.
- **401 Unauthorized:** check your username and password in the vault. The Postman Console shows each login and refresh.

# Learn more

- [Documentation](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/) and [API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/), including account limits and every response field
- [Status page](https://status.enterprise.wikimedia.com/) and support through [your dashboard](https://dashboard.enterprise.wikimedia.com/)
- [Report a problem with this collection](https://github.com/wikimedia-enterprise/postman/issues) on GitHub
- [Contact us](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/contact/) to talk about a paid account

# **License**

Copyright 2026 Wikimedia, LLC. Licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0).

This tool is not covered under Wikimedia Enterprise SLA.

Content returned by the APIs comes from Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects and keeps its own license, which each article states in its `license` field.

item.name: Authentication

exec: // Sends the body as JSON, built with JSON.stringify so a password with quotes or backslashes stays valid.
// The body shown below is what this script replaces. Outside the Postman app, it reads the
// wmeUsername and wmePassword variables instead of the vault.
const value = typeof pm.vault !== "undefined" ? await pm.vault.get(name) : undefined;
// No vault access: fall back to variables, as outside the Postman app.
// Saves the tokens in the same collection variables the collection pre-request script uses.

request.description:
Create new access, id, and refresh tokens with your valid username and password.

The access token lasts 24 hours. When it runs out, use the refresh token with **Refresh Token** to get a new one. Log in again when the refresh token expires after 90 days or has been used 90 times.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/authentication/POST/v1/login)

exec: // Sends the body as JSON, built with JSON.stringify. The body shown below is what this script replaces.
// Outside the Postman app, it reads the wmeUsername variable instead of the vault.
const value = typeof pm.vault !== "undefined" ? await pm.vault.get(name) : undefined;
// No vault access: fall back to variables, as outside the Postman app.
// Saves the tokens in the same collection variables the collection pre-request script uses.

request.description:
Provides new access and id tokens with your valid username and refresh token.

Refresh returns a new access token but no new refresh token, so keep using the one from **Login**.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/authentication/POST/v1/token-refresh)

Revokes your refresh token and the access tokens issued from it.

Afterwards the collection clears its stored tokens, so the next request logs in again.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/authentication/POST/v1/token-revoke)

exec: // The stored tokens no longer work, so clear them; the next request logs in again.

request.description:
Changes your password, using your access token, your current password, and the new one.

This endpoint takes the access token in the request body (`access_token`), not in the `Authorization` header.

After changing your password, update the `wmePassword` secret in your Postman Vault.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/authentication/POST/v1/change-password)

Emails you a confirmation code. Use it with **Forgot Password Confirmation** to set a new password.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/authentication/POST/v1/forgot-password)

Sets a new password, using your username, the `confirmation_code` emailed by **Forgot Password**, and the new password.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/authentication/POST/v1/forgot-password-confirm)

Sets a new password when **Login** answers with the `NEW_PASSWORD_REQUIRED` challenge. Send your username, the `session` from the Login response, and the new password.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/authentication/POST/v1/new-password-required)

item.description:
Log in, refresh and revoke tokens, and manage your password. Use your Wikimedia Enterprise username in lowercase.

Access tokens last 24 hours and refresh tokens last 90 days; each refresh token can be used up to 90 times. The collection logs in and refreshes for you, so you only need these requests to manage your tokens or password yourself.

[Authentication docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/authentication/)

Reference data for building requests: project codes, languages, projects, and namespaces. Use these identifiers to filter results by project or language and to read article responses.

[Metadata docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/)

item.name: Snapshot API

request.description:
Returns a list of available project snapshots by namespace. Includes identifiers, file sizes and other relevant metadata.

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots)

Information on a specific snapshot bundle. Includes identifiers, file sizes and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{snapshot_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots/{identifier})

header.description: Optional byte range, for example `bytes=0-1048575`. Send it to the presigned URL to resume a partial download.

request.description:
Downloadable bundle of all current revisions in a specified project and namespace.

Returns `307 Temporary Redirect`. This request doesn't follow the redirect, because the files are large: copy the URL from the `Location` header (the response body shows it as a link too) and download it within 60 seconds, for example with `curl --location`. Don't send your access token to that URL.

To check the size first, send **Snapshot Download Headers**. To resume a large download, see [Resumable downloads](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/#resumable-downloads).

Required: `{{snapshot_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/GET/v2/snapshots/{identifier}/download)

Returns only the headers of the download: file size (`Content-Length`), `Last-Modified`, `ETag` and `Accept-Ranges`. Use it to check a file before downloading it, or to plan ranged downloads.

Required: `{{snapshot_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/HEAD/v2/snapshots/{identifier}/download)

Returns a list of available chunks for a specific snapshot. Includes chunk identifiers and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{snapshot_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots/{identifier}/chunks)

Information on a specific chunk of a snapshot. Includes chunk identifier, size, and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{snapshot_identifier}}`, `{{chunk_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots/{snapshot_identifier}/chunks/{chunk_identifier})

header.description: Optional byte range, for example `bytes=0-1048575`. Send it to the presigned URL to resume a partial download.

request.description:
Downloadable bundle of a specific chunk from a snapshot. Returns a zipped tar file.

Returns `307 Temporary Redirect`. This request doesn't follow the redirect, because the files are large: copy the URL from the `Location` header (the response body shows it as a link too) and download it within 60 seconds, for example with `curl --location`. Don't send your access token to that URL.

To check the size first, send **Snapshot Chunk Download Headers**. To resume a large download, see [Resumable downloads](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/#resumable-downloads).

Required: `{{snapshot_identifier}}`, `{{chunk_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/GET/v2/snapshots/{snapshot_identifier}/chunks/{chunk_identifier}/download)

Returns only the headers of the download: file size (`Content-Length`), `Last-Modified`, `ETag` and `Accept-Ranges`. Use it to check a file before downloading it, or to plan ranged downloads.

Required: `{{snapshot_identifier}}`, `{{chunk_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/snapshots/HEAD/v2/snapshots/{snapshot_identifier}/chunks/{chunk_identifier}/download)

item.description:
Snapshots of Structured Contents: each article's abstract, description, main image, infobox, sections, lists, citations, references, and tables, parsed into JSON.

[Structured Contents](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/api/structured-contents/)

item.name: Wikidata Snapshots (Beta)
item.description:
Wikidata has its own snapshots: `items` (every current item in the main Wikidata graph) and `properties` (every current property). Each is one NDJSON file in a compressed tarball, split into chunks for parallel downloads.

[Snapshot API docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/)

request.description:
Returns the list of available Wikidata snapshots, currently `items` and `properties`. Includes identifiers, file sizes, record counts, and other relevant metadata.

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots/wikidata)

Information on the Wikidata `items` or `properties` snapshot. Includes identifier, file size, record count, chunk identifiers, and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{wikidata_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots/wikidata/{identifier})

header.description: Optional byte range, for example `bytes=0-1048575`. Send it to the presigned URL to resume a partial download.

request.description:
Downloadable bundle of every current item in the Wikidata Main Graph (`items`) or every current property (`properties`), as one NDJSON file in a compressed tarball.

Returns `307 Temporary Redirect`. This request doesn't follow the redirect, because the files are large: copy the URL from the `Location` header (the response body shows it as a link too) and download it within 60 seconds, for example with `curl --location`. Don't send your access token to that URL.

To check the size first, send **Wikidata Snapshot Download Headers (Beta)**. To resume a large download, see [Resumable downloads](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/#resumable-downloads).

Required: `{{wikidata_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/GET/v2/snapshots/wikidata/{identifier}/download)

Returns only the headers of the download: file size (`Content-Length`), `Last-Modified`, `ETag` and `Accept-Ranges`. Use it to check a file before downloading it, or to plan ranged downloads.

Required: `{{wikidata_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/HEAD/v2/snapshots/wikidata/{identifier}/download)

Returns a list of available chunks for the Wikidata `items` or `properties` snapshot. Includes chunk identifiers and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{wikidata_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots/wikidata/{identifier}/chunks)

Information on a specific chunk of the Wikidata `items` or `properties` snapshot. Includes chunk identifier, size, and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{wikidata_identifier}}`, `{{wikidata_chunk_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/POST/v2/snapshots/wikidata/{identifier}/chunks/{chunk_identifier})

header.description: Optional byte range, for example `bytes=0-1048575`. Send it to the presigned URL to resume a partial download.

request.description:
Downloadable bundle of a specific chunk from the Wikidata `items` or `properties` snapshot. Returns a zipped tar file.

Returns `307 Temporary Redirect`. This request doesn't follow the redirect, because the files are large: copy the URL from the `Location` header (the response body shows it as a link too) and download it within 60 seconds, for example with `curl --location`. Don't send your access token to that URL.

To check the size first, send **Wikidata Snapshot Chunk Download Headers (Beta)**. To resume a large download, see [Resumable downloads](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/#resumable-downloads).

Required: `{{wikidata_identifier}}`, `{{wikidata_chunk_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/GET/v2/snapshots/wikidata/{identifier}/chunks/{chunk_identifier}/download)

Returns only the headers of the download: file size (`Content-Length`), `Last-Modified`, `ETag` and `Accept-Ranges`. Use it to check a file before downloading it, or to plan ranged downloads.

Required: `{{wikidata_identifier}}`, `{{wikidata_chunk_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-snapshots/HEAD/v2/snapshots/wikidata/{identifier}/chunks/{chunk_identifier}/download)

item.description:
Download an entire Wikimedia project, such as English Wikipedia or French Wiktionary, as a compressed tarball (`.tar.gz`) holding one NDJSON file with every article. How often snapshots update depends on your account; the docs have the details. Use the **Metadata** requests to find the identifier you need, and chunks to split a large download.

Snapshots can contain a small number of duplicate or deleted articles. When an article appears more than once, keep the copy with the highest `version.identifier`.

[Snapshot API docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/) and [data dictionary](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/data-dictionary/)

item.name: On-demand API

request.description:
Most current revision of an article.

Required: `{{articlename}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/articles/POST/v2/articles/{name})

response.name: NASA in English Wikipedia, select fields

request.description:
Structured Contents extracts infoboxes, sections, tables, references, and more from raw wikitext and HTML and delivers them as structured, machine-readable JSON.

Returns the Structured Contents of the current version of an article.

Required: `{{articlename}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/structured-contents/POST/v2/structured-contents/{name})

response.name: NASA in English Wikipedia, select fields

item.name: Wikidata (Beta)

request.description:
Returns data and metadata about the last revision of a given Wikidata Item identifier (Q-number, e.g. Q42). Only gives access to the Main Wikidata graph.

Required: `{{wikidata_item_id}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/items/{identifier})

response.name: Douglas Adams (Q42)

request.description:
Returns data and metadata about the last revision of a given Wikidata Property identifier (P-number, e.g. P31).

Required: `{{wikidata_property_id}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/properties/{identifier})

Returns the entity's label in every language, as one object keyed by language code. Works for items (Q-numbers, main Wikidata graph only) and properties (P-numbers).

Required: `{{wikidata_entity_id}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/labels/{identifier})

item.description:
Look up Wikidata items (Q-numbers, such as Q42) and properties (P-numbers, such as P31), or list an entity's labels in every language.

[Wikidata lookup docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/#wikidata-item-lookup-beta)

Look up the current version of an article by name across all [supported projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/), or narrow the results with [filters and fields](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/filtering/). Responses are JSON by default; send `Accept: application/x-ndjson` for NDJSON. **Structured Contents Article Lookup (Beta)** returns the article's infobox, sections, and more as parsed JSON.

[On-demand API docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/)

item.name: Realtime API

request.description:
Returns a stream of article updates, deletions, and visibility changes across all supported projects. Each event's type is in its `event.type` field: `update`, `delete`, or `visibility-change`.

The Realtime API requires a paid account. On a free account, this request returns `403 Forbidden`.

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/realtime-articles/POST/v2/articles)

response.name: Selected fields

request.description:
Returns a stream of Wikidata item updates, deletions, and visibility changes in real-time.

The Realtime API requires a paid account.

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/realtime-wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata)

item.name: Realtime: Batch

request.description:
Returns a list of available Realtime: Batch files by date and hour (00, 01, ..., 23). Includes identifiers, file sizes and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{date}}`, `{{hour}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/batches/POST/v2/batches/{date}/{hour})

Information on a specific Realtime: Batch file. Includes identifier, file size and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{date}}`, `{{hour}}`, `{{snapshot_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/batches/POST/v2/batches/{date}/{hour}/{identifier})

header.description: Optional byte range, for example `bytes=0-1048575`. Send it to the presigned URL to resume a partial download.

request.description:
Downloadable bundle of updated articles by project, namespace, date, and hour. Generated hourly starting at 00:00 UTC each day.

Returns `307 Temporary Redirect`. This request doesn't follow the redirect, because the files are large: copy the URL from the `Location` header (the response body shows it as a link too) and download it within 60 seconds, for example with `curl --location`. Don't send your access token to that URL.

To check the size first, send **Hourly Batch File Download Headers**. To resume a large download, see [Resumable downloads](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/#resumable-downloads).

Required: `{{date}}`, `{{hour}}`, `{{snapshot_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/batches/GET/v2/batches/{date}/{hour}/{identifier}/download)

Returns only the headers of the download: file size (`Content-Length`), `Last-Modified`, `ETag` and `Accept-Ranges`. Use it to check a file before downloading it, or to plan ranged downloads.

Required: `{{date}}`, `{{hour}}`, `{{snapshot_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/batches/HEAD/v2/batches/{date}/{hour}/{identifier}/download)

Returns a list of available Wikidata Realtime: Batch files by date and hour (00, 01, ..., 23). Includes identifiers, file sizes and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{date}}`, `{{hour}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-batches/POST/v2/batches/{date}/{hour}/wikidata)

Information on the hourly Wikidata `items` or `properties` batch for a given date and hour. Includes identifier, file size and other relevant metadata.

Required: `{{date}}`, `{{hour}}`, `{{wikidata_identifier}}`

Also available as `GET`, with `fields` and `filters` sent as query parameters.

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-batches/POST/v2/batches/{date}/{hour}/wikidata/{identifier})

header.description: Optional byte range, for example `bytes=0-1048575`. Send it to the presigned URL to resume a partial download.

request.description:
Downloadable bundle of the Wikidata items or properties updated in a given date and hour. Generated hourly starting at 00:00 UTC each day.

Returns `307 Temporary Redirect`. This request doesn't follow the redirect, because the files are large: copy the URL from the `Location` header (the response body shows it as a link too) and download it within 60 seconds, for example with `curl --location`. Don't send your access token to that URL.

To check the size first, send **Wikidata Hourly Batch File Download Headers (Beta)**. To resume a large download, see [Resumable downloads](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/#resumable-downloads).

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-batches/GET/v2/batches/{date}/{hour}/wikidata/{identifier}/download)

item.name: Wikidata Hourly Batch File Download Headers (Beta)

request.description:
Returns only the headers of the download: file size (`Content-Length`), `Last-Modified`, `ETag` and `Accept-Ranges`. Use it to check a file before downloading it, or to plan ranged downloads.

Required: `{{date}}`, `{{hour}}`, `{{wikidata_identifier}}`

[API reference](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata-batches/HEAD/v2/batches/{date}/{hour}/wikidata/{identifier}/download)

item.description:
Each hour's updates as downloadable files, generated hourly from 00:00 UTC. Use them to stay current without keeping a stream open. Like the rest of the Realtime API, Realtime: Batch requires a paid account.

[Realtime API docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/realtime/)

Receive updates from all [supported projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/) as they happen, through a stream or hourly **Realtime: Batch** files. The Realtime API requires a paid account; [contact us](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/contact/) for access.

Streams send server-sent events by default, or NDJSON with the `Accept: application/x-ndjson` header. Each event has one of three types:

- `update`: an article was created, its content changed, or its name or namespace changed.
- `delete`: an article was deleted.
- `visibility-change`: community volunteers changed the visibility of an article's editor, comment, or content.

[Realtime API docs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/realtime/)

exec: * Wikimedia Enterprise APIs: automatic login and token refresh.
* Runs before every request except those sent to the auth server (the Authentication folder).
* It logs in when there is no token, refreshes the access token an hour before it expires, and
* logs in again when the refresh token is near its 90-day limit or a refresh fails.
*  1. Add your Wikimedia Enterprise username and password to your Postman Vault as the secrets
*  2. Let scripts read the vault: in the Vault, open Settings and turn on "Allow Vault secrets
*     in scripts". If Postman asks, allow this collection.
* Credentials are only sent to the collection variable `auth_server`, which must be an https://
* URL. An environment or global variable with the same name is ignored here.
* Tokens and their expiry times are kept in collection variables, so no environment is needed.
* Outside the Postman app (Newman, Postman CLI), pass wmeUsername and wmePassword as environment
throw new Error("The collection variable auth_server must be an https:// URL, so the collection doesn't send credentials anywhere else.");
console.warn("Ignoring auth_server from your environment or globals: credentials only go to the collection's own auth_server.");
? `Postman did not let this script read the vault (${vaultError}). In the vault, open Settings and turn on "Allow Vault secrets in scripts".`
: "Add wmeUsername and wmePassword to your Postman Vault, spelled exactly like that.";
throw new Error(`Wikimedia Enterprise credentials not found. ${reason} See the collection overview.`);
const response = await send("/v1/login", { username, password });
throw new Error(`Login failed with HTTP ${response.code}. Check the wmeUsername and wmePassword vault secrets.`);
const challenge = body.challenge_name ? ` It asked for ${body.challenge_name} first; finish that with the Authentication requests, then send this request again.` : "";
throw new Error(`Login returned no access token.${challenge}`);
const response = await send("/v1/token-refresh", { username, refresh_token: refreshToken });
console.warn(`Token refresh failed with HTTP ${response.code}; logging in again.`);
console.warn("Token refresh returned no access token; logging in again.");
// Earlier versions of this collection kept tokens in the active environment, where they would
// override the collection variables this script now uses.
console.log("Removed token variables left in the environment by an earlier version of this collection.");
